etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English anniversary, from Medieval Latin anniversāria (diēs), anniversārium, from anniversārius (“yearly”), from annus (“year”) + versus, past participle of vertere (“to turn”).

definitions.definition: (especially) Such a day that commemorates a wedding.
A day that is an exact number of years (to the day) since a given significant event occurred. Often preceded by an ordinal number indicating the number of years.
(loosely) A day subsequent in time to a given event by some significant period other than a year (especially as prefixed by the amount of time in question).

quote.citation: 1984 February 27, “Never Mind the Tranquil Facade”, in Time:
quote.text: The occasion was the six-month anniversary of the Aug. 8 coup that brought General Óscar Humberto Mejía Victores to power.

In a thinly veiled threat to Saddam Hussein, President George Bush marked the six-month anniversary of September 11th by reiterating America's commitment to prevent rogue countries obtaining weapons of mass destruction.

quote.citation: 2006, DB Schrock, Soulmonger Dot Com, page 28:
quote.text: Jonathon proposed to his [Jess's] mom on their three-month anniversary of meeting and married her on their fourth.
